diagnostic_evidence.quote: due to the supremum over the initialization $\param_{0}$ in \eqref{eq:Neps}

issues.failure_explanation: N_eps is defined with a supremum over all theta_0 in Theta. The constants M_1, M_2 come from part (i) and contain A=f(theta_0)-f^* and the Lipschitz constant L on a compact set built from the sublevel set at level f(theta_0)+T. Both grow with theta_0, and Theta may be unbounded. So the stated bound is not uniform in theta_0, and the supremum can be infinite. Part (ii) is derived from (i) with theta_0-dependent constants, which supports only an initialization-dependent bound.

failure_location.quote: Then the worst-case iteration complexity $N_{\eps}$ for Algorithm \ref{algorithm:BMM-DR} satisfies $N_{\eps} = O(\eps^{-2} (\log \eps^{-1})^{2} )$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define N_eps with the supremum over initializations in a fixed sublevel set (or compact set), or state that the constant depends on theta_0. Then M_1 and M_2 are uniform over that set.
issues.overall_effect: The 'worst-case over all initializations' complexity claim, repeated in the abstract and the corollaries, is unsupported as stated. The per-initialization bound remains valid.
issues.title: Worst-case complexity taken over all initializations, but constants depend on the initialization
issues.why_classification: The repair is short but weakens the advertised uniform worst-case guarantee to a restricted-initialization one. The result stays recognizably comparable.

The proof also cites conditions (a)/(b) of Prop. non-stationary_nbh in swapped roles, and (b) concerns theta_n^star, not theta_n. issues.failure_explanation: h>=0 on Theta^(i) with h(theta_{n-1})=0 only gives <nabla h(theta_{n-1}), theta-theta_{n-1}> >= 0 on Theta^(i). Zero gradient follows only if theta_{n-1}^(i) is interior. Counterexample: Theta=[0,inf), f=0, g(theta)=theta at theta_{n-1}=0. Surrogates satisfying the listed properties (1)-(3) need not be tangent to f on the boundary, which is exactly where NMF and other constrained iterates sit. The lemma and later results use tangency (nabla g = nabla f, nabla h(theta_{n-1})=0).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $g_{n}\ge f_{n}$ and $g_{n}(H_{n})=f_{n}(H_{n})$; $g_{n}$ is a quadratic function.

issues.failure_explanation: g_n is defined by expansion at h_n (with D and the rho-term centered accordingly). The gradient used to derive the MUR update expands at tilde h_n = h_n v delta. With expansion at h_n the minimizer is a gradient step from h_n, not the MUR formula. With expansion at tilde h_n, g_n(H_n) = f_n(H_n) fails whenever some entry of H_n is below delta, which can happen after an update. Then sharpness (property (2)) fails and monotonicity is not guaranteed. So the points the corollary relies on are not jointly valid, and MUR is not shown to be a BMM instance. The W-update displayed also has inconsistencies (tilde W_n defined from itself, and H_n used instead of H_{n+1}).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the surrogate consistently at the algorithm's expansion point and restore sharpness. For example, constrain H >= delta so that tilde H_n = H_n, or modify the surrogate/update so that sharpness, majorization and the closed-form minimizer hold simultaneously. Then re-verify A3-A5.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary NMF (and the MUR option of the NCPD corollary) is not derived from Theorem 2.1 as written.
issues.title: MUR update is not the minimizer of the stated surrogate, and the surrogate is not sharp at H_n
issues.why_classification: A contained redefinition of the algorithm or constraint is needed, with re-verification of the surrogate properties. The overall conclusion is comparable and the architecture is unchanged.

The $C^{1}$-assumption of the objective in \ref{assumption:A2} is weaker than the $L$-smoothness assumption

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 2.1 needs a surrogate that majorizes f_n^(i) on all of Theta^(i) and, for r_n=infinity, the quadratic gap bound of A3(b) with rho>0. A2 gives only local Lipschitz continuity of the gradient on compacts. On an unbounded Theta (e.g., f=theta^4 on R) no prox-linear surrogate with finite lambda majorizes f globally. Even with global L, lambda = L gives rho=0 and the lower bound of A3(b) fails; one needs lambda > L strictly.
